ABOUT THIS ROLE

As Ashby’s first Demo Engineer, you’ll own the systems that make our demo environments reliable, current, and tailored — the infrastructure the entire go-to-market team leans on to show Ashby at its best. Today, AEs and SEs maintain and configure their own demo accounts by hand. That doesn’t scale: reps lose selling time, demos drift out of date, and every new product release widens the gap between what Ashby can do and what we can actually show live. Your job is to close that gap.

This is a net-new role. Right now, the work is split between ad hoc effort and a new set of disposable demo templates the Internal Platform team is building. You’ll own the layer on top of that foundation — customizing and extending those templates, generating realistic demo data, tailoring environments for specific verticals and new markets, and making sure every feature is demoable before it ships. You’ll sit within Solutions Engineering, reporting to the Global Head of Solutions Engineering, and partner closely with Internal Platform and Product teams.

Your work will be split roughly 70/30: about 70% owning, customizing, and extending the demo template system and the data and content inside it, and about 30% running demo readiness as a program — release readiness, documentation, and enablement so the GTM team always has current, credible demos to work with.

The best person for this job is genuinely hands-on technical — working with internal tools and configuration files, using APIs, and general data preparation — who gets energy from building leverage for a whole team rather than fixing one demo at a time.

YOU COULD BE A GREAT FIT IF:

 - 🛠 You’re comfortable working in JSON, calling REST / developer APIs, using AI tools, and scripting to configure and customize environments.

 - 🏗 You’re a builder, not just an operator. You get energy from creating systems and tooling that make a whole team more effective over time.

 - 🎥 You care deeply about demo quality. You understand what makes a product demo land, and you’re thoughtful about data realism and the narrative a demo needs to support.

 - 🧠 You have strong product intuition and can learn a deeply configurable product quickly, understanding how the different pieces connect.

 - 🔁 You have an iterative mindset. You like testing what works, refining over time, and improving based on what you learn from the field.

 - 🧩 You’re a systems thinker who would rather standardize and automate than manually repeat the same setup.

 - ⚡ You’re comfortable with ambiguity and enjoy a 0→1 role where the infrastructure is still being built around you.

 - 🤝 You partner well cross-functionally — with Engineering and with GTM — and can translate their needs into reliable systems.

You’ll define a role that doesn’t exist yet. This is a net-new role designed around a real business need. You won’t inherit a mature playbook — you’ll build the infrastructure that lets the whole GTM team demo at a higher level.

You’ll sit at the intersection of Engineering and GTM. This is a rare blend of technical building and understanding what the field actually needs. You’ll help translate our product releases into live deals — and connect the two.

 Build the team (first 180 days). Hire, onboard, and ramp a new cohort of BDRs with clear ramp plans and productivity targets. Then build the capacity model that tells us when and where to add more BDRs and AEs through 2027.

 Job Title: Research Assistant (1 position)  
 Location: Max Bell School of Public Policy, McGill University  
 Supervisor: Siobhan Harty, Slater Family Visiting Scholar    
 Start Date: Late November 2026 (as soon as possible)  
 End Date: July 9, 2027  
 Hours: 2–4 hours per week   
 Rate: $25.00/hour  
 Project Title  
 Second Century Commission   
 Position Summary  
 Siobhan Harty, Slater Family Visiting Scholar at the Max Bell School of Public Policy and Research Director for the Second Century Commission, is seeking one Research Assistant (RA) to support the work of the Commission. The Second Century Commission ( Second Century Commission on Canada–US Relations ) is a binational initiative focused on Canada–U.S. relations for the second century of formal diplomatic relations beginning in 2026. Under the leadership of co-chairs Lisa Raitt and Jane Harman, the binational Commission will bring together approximately twenty prominent Canadians and Americans to develop a forward-looking agenda for relations between the two countries. Commissioners include former Cabinet members, governors, provincial premiers, leading business executives, leaders in philanthropy, experts in AI and digital technology, defence and security leaders, among others. The Commission is led by the Max Bell School, the Johns Hopkins School of Advanced International Studies, and the Centre for International Governance Innovation. Following the first in-person meeting of Commissioners in Baltimore on October 21, the Commission will continue to meet over the next year to deliberate on policy recommendations and develop a report for policy makers in Canada and the United States. Commissioners are supported by expert research papers and other analysis and engagement activities. The RA will help organize the meetings of the Commissioners, support the Research Director to manage the production of research papers, conduct research to support the Commission as required and play an integral role in shaping the Youth Assembly. This position is an opportunity to be part of an initiative that demonstrates how public policy is influenced from outside government by leading voices.  
 Key Responsibilities  
 Organize regularly scheduled meetings of the organizing team for the Commission, take meeting notes and track deliverables.  
 Play a leading role on the Max Bell team that will organize the next in-person meeting of the Commission in Montreal (Spring 2027), including agenda, meeting products and logistics.  
 Support management of research papers through fact-checking, citation management, and initial editing in line with a style guide.   
 Maintain a monthly list of reading materials for the Commissioners.  
 Conduct research as required to support the Commissioners, for public use on the Commission’s website and other outputs.   
 Play a leading role in the development of a Youth Assembly that will run independently alongside the Commission and provide Commissioners with a youth perspective.  
 Qualifications  
 Strong analytical research and writing skills in English; French is an asset.  
 Highly organized, pays attention to details and is able to track deliverables.  
 Interest in Canada-US relations and the major policy areas shaping the relationship.   
 Comfortable researching contemporary and historical issues using a range of tools and sources.   
 Careful attention to sourcing, nuance, accuracy, and competing interpretations.  
 Ability to organize research systematically and work independently.  
 Experience with academic databases, citation management, and responsible use of AI-supported research tools is an asset.  
 Must be a current MPP student at the Max Bell School of Public Policy.

 Please submit a CV and brief statement of interest through McGill Workday.

Job Description: 
 The Manager, Backup Storage & Data Resilience provides specialized 2LOD oversight and challenge of backup strategy, storage resilience, data recoverability, cyber recovery readiness, and recovery testing evidence. The role evaluates whether critical systems, applications, and data can be restored reliably within tolerance windows under severe but plausible disruption scenarios, including ransomware or data corruption events.
 Reporting to the Director, Regulatory and Subsidiary Reporting, the Manager, Regulatory and Subsidiary Reporting will be part of the Retail Advice & Solutions Finance team and will be responsible for all aspects of financial reporting processes related to the mutual fund dealer Sun Life Financial Investment Services (Canada) Inc. (SLFISI), investment dealer Sun Life Canada Securities Inc. (SLCSI) and insurance distributor Sun Life Financial Distributors Inc. (SLFDI).This encompasses accounting and regulatory reporting for SLFISI and SLCSI in compliance with Canadian Investment Regulatory Organization (CIRO) rules. The large scale and scope of this role requires a high level of accounting knowledge, controls and processes, analytical insight, and operational efficiency.
 What will you do? 
 Backup & Data Recoverability Challenge 
 Review and challenge backup strategy, coverage, frequency, retention, storage architecture, immutable/air-gapped backup practices, and alignment to criticality and recovery objectives.
 Assess whether backup and recovery capabilities are risk-based, complete, tested, and aligned to critical operation tolerances and RTO/RPO requirements.
 Identify gaps in data resilience, backup coverage, cyber recovery readiness, restore success rates, and evidence quality.
 Review backup and recoverability capabilities for cloud, hybrid, SaaS, and third-party technology services supporting critical operations.
 Challenge recovery dependencies, concentration risks, and recovery assumptions that may affect data restoration.
 Assess resilience and currency of backup platforms, recovery tooling, and recovery access controls.
 Recoverability Testing & Evidence Validation 
 Challenge the scope, frequency, and adequacy of backup recovery testing, including critical applications, databases, infrastructure services, and cyber/ransomware recovery scenarios.
 Review evidence supporting restore capability, data integrity, recovery timing, test exceptions, failed restores, and remediation closure.
 Escalate material concerns where data recoverability is not demonstrated or where recovery assumptions are unsupported by evidence through established issue and governance processes.
 Risk Monitoring, Metrics & Reporting 
 Contribute to KRIs and risk appetite measures related to backup coverage, restore performance, recoverability testing, cyber recovery readiness, data integrity, and unresolved gaps.
 Provide insights for senior governance reporting on backup/data resilience posture, trends, root causes, and remediation progress.
 Maintain challenge records, issue linkages, and evidence documentation suitable for audit, regulatory, and management review.
 Identify recurring recoverability issues, emerging risks, and dependency concerns affecting backup, data resilience, and cyber recovery capabilities requiring leadership & stakeholder attention.
 Partnership & Improvement 
 Partner with DBTS, Cyber, Technology Resilience, Operational Resilience, BCM, TPRM, and Business Group stakeholders to ensure backup/data resilience is integrated into end-to-end resilience outcomes.
 Using validations and evidence review, continually look for & recommend practical improvements to recovery strategy, evidence standards, testing playbooks, prioritization criteria, and issue closure expectations.
 Support technology resilience reviews for major changes, cloud transformation, or new platforms where backup/data recoverability could affect critical operations.
 Observe integrated recovery exercises to assess the effectiveness of end-to-end data recoverability outcomes.
 Expected Outcomes / Measures of Success 
 Evidence of independently validated recoverability of critical systems, applications, and data.
 Backup and cyber recovery capabilities are tested and reviewed on a risk-based basis and linked to business tolerances.·   Observed material gaps in backup coverage, restore success, data integrity, or cyber recovery readiness are formally captured and escalated.
 Management reporting provides meaningful visibility into recoverability risk and remediation progress.
 What do you need to succeed? 
 Experience with backup and storage architecture, data recoverability, restore testing, immutable and air-gapped backups, cyber recovery, ransomware scenarios, database/application recovery, and technology risk.
 Understanding of operational resilience, BCM/DR lifecycle, E-21, B-13, risk appetite, KRIs, issue management, and independent 2LOD challenge expectations.
 Ability to review technical evidence, identify recoverability gaps, and translate technical weaknesses into resilience risk and remediation needs.
 Strong analytical, documentation, stakeholder management, and constructive challenge skills.
 University degree or equivalent combination of education and experience.
 Typically 7+ years of experience in backup/storage, technology recovery, cyber recovery, technology risk, operational resilience, disaster recovery, or related fields.
 Professional certifications or training in cloud resilience, storage/backup platforms, cyber recovery, CRISC, CISM, CISSP, CBCP/MBCI, ITIL, DRI/BCI, or equivalent are assets.

 We’re proud to be recognized as a company with a 2026 Most Trusted Executive team by Great Place to  Work® Canada
 Access to short-term assignments or ‘Gigs’ across the organization, to help you develop new skills and connections.

 Care Days available for self-care or care of others (i.e., family or others you may support) and Sick Days to  support your well-being.

 Set up and maintain assigned projects in InEight and Vista, ensuring project budgets, cost codes, contract values, and billing arrangements align with approved estimates and contract requirements.

 Our AI agent now answers repeatable, well-documented questions.  You are your clients' person inside the company: an internal support person who also works like an account manager. You onboard them, check in before they need to ask, solve problems with our developers when something breaks, and help them use more of what we offer.

 Own your accounts

 Get clients to real proficiency with the product, not just past their immediate question

 Treat client sentiment as the real measure of success, not ticket speed
 Look for small moments to go above and beyond, and share what works so it becomes how the whole team operates
 Support your accounts

 Get on a call when a situation needs a human voice

 Check on your open Linear issues, chase what is stuck, and confirm the fix with the client

À propos d'Elia
elia est une plateforme SaaS B2B de gestion de l'espace de travail qui aide les entreprises à réinventer leur environnement de travail : réservation de bureaux et de salles, gestion des visiteurs, capteurs IoT et occupation, gestion d'actifs, affichage numérique, casiers intelligents, et plus encore. Nos clients incluent de grandes organisations à travers le Canada, les États-Unis et quelques autres pays.
Nous sommes une équipe technique, en pleine croissance, où chaque personne a un impact direct sur le produit et où l'IA fait partie intégrante de notre façon de construire.
 
Le rôle
Nous cherchons une développeur·euse full stack pour rejoindre notre équipe de développement et faire évoluer lʼensemble de la plateforme elia. Vous ferez partie d'une cellule compacte de 4 développeurs, 1 Product Owner et 1 Product Designer, et travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec le CTO et le reste de l'équipe pour livrer le code de qualité, déployé en production à tous les jours.
On cherche quelqu'un qui fait avancer l'équipe : qui pose les bonnes questions, qui n'a pas peur de challenger nos décisions (ni de se faire challenger), qui veut continuellement apprendre et sʼaméliorer.
 
Responsabilités
Participer activement aux décisions sur les fonctionnalités à développer et lʼarchitecture à mettre en place pour y arriver.
Développer de nouvelles fonctionnalités dans la plateforme elia, du front-end au back-end, en assurant la qualité et la pérennité du code.
Effectuer les revues de code.
Déployer l'application en production, la surveiller, la maintenir et régler les incidents
Proposer des solutions d'amélioration continue pour l'efficacité de l'équipe et l'expérience développeur.
Prendre partie aux décisions sur les processus à intégrer et aider à les mettre en place.
 
Profil recherché
Minimum 3 ans d'expérience en développement dʼapplication web
BAC en génie logiciel ou informatique ou formation en développement web (AEC, DEC)
Excellentes connaissances de React, TypeScript, Kotlin/Java
Bonnes connaissances de SQL (PostgreSQL), CSS (Tailwind)
Avoir à cœur la qualité du code et les bonnes pratiques de développement (SOLID, TDD, etc.)
Être capable de travailler dans un environnement Cloud avec AWS
Curiosité technique, toujours vouloir en apprendre plus, à sʼaméliorer
Capacité à synthétiser de l'information complexe et à la vulgariser
À l'aise avec l'IA
Chez Elia, l'IA fait partie intégrante de notre façon de travailler. On ne cherche pas à vous convaincre que l'IA accélère le développement. En partie du principe que vous le savez déjà. Ce qu'on recherche :
Vous utilisez déjà Claude (ou un outil équivalent) au quotidien, pas seulement pour écrire du code, mais pour repenser votre façon de travailler ;
Vous êtes capable de nous montrer une façon différente de faire les choses, pas seulement de suivre le mouvement ;
 
Ce que nous offrons
Chez elia, tu auras l'opportunité de :
Travailler dans une équipe dynamique en pleine croissance;
Vivre l'expérience « start-up » ;
Profiter d'un horaire flexible et d'une possibilité de travail 100% télétravail ou hybride (Montréal ou Québec);

 About us 
 Role information 
 Blobby Media is looking for an organized, reliable Production Manager to run the operations behind our shorts. Every short moves through a 12-weekday pipeline (script, voice, audio, storyboard, animation and final edit), with a new batch starting every weekday. You'll own that schedule and make sure every short ships on time.
 You'll work directly with our founder and Creative Director: he owns the creative, you own operations. As we scale to 35 shorts a week, you'll make sure the pipeline, the team and the budget keep up.
 Your duties will include 
 • Running the daily production schedule and tracking every short through every stage, with dozens in progress at any time
 • Holding the team to deadlines across time zones, spotting delays early and reassigning work when someone falls behind
 • Sourcing, onboarding and offboarding contractors, and keeping backups ready to step in
 • Making sure contractors are paid correctly and on time, based on our rate card
 • Reviewing every final cut before release and sending notes to the editor until it's approved
 • Scheduling approved shorts on YouTube and coordinating with our distribution partner, who releases them on all major platforms
 • Protecting the schedule from late changes once scripts, audio and storyboards are locked
 • Tracking capacity, costs and turnaround times, and reporting on what's working and what isn't
 • Planning headcount as we scale, and helping promote team members into lead roles
 • Documenting and improving our processes as the pipeline grows
 • Keeping scripts, audio and unreleased shorts confidential
 A successful candidate will have 
 • Experience running production for animation, video or another deadline-driven content pipeline
 • A track record of managing remote freelancers or contractors across time zones
 • Strong organization: you build the tracker, keep it current and always know where everything stands
 • Comfort with numbers: budgets, rate cards, capacity planning and spreadsheets
 • The confidence to hold people to deadlines and push back when a change would break the schedule, even on the founder
 • A sharp eye for detail when checking finished videos
 • Clear, proactive communication in English
 • A home base in Canada and the legal right to work here
 Bonus skills 
 • Experience at a YouTube channel or animation studio producing at high volume
 • Hands-on knowledge of how 2D animation gets made
 • Experience hiring for and scaling a creative team
 • Experience paying international contractors
 • Production tracking tools like Notion, Airtable or Kitsu
 Pay and benefits 
 • $90,000 CAD base salary
 • Health, dental and vision benefits
 • 3 weeks of paid vacation, plus statutory holidays
 • 5 paid sick days
 • Performance and salary reviews every 6 months
 What we offer 
 • Full-time and fully remote within Canada, 40 hours a week, Monday to Friday. We measure your results and output, not your hours.
 • Working directly with our founder
 • Real ownership: the schedule, the tools and the processes are yours to build and improve
 • The shorts you ship seen by millions of people in every major language
 • Room to grow as the studio scales
 Our values 
 We hire on skill, reliability and overall passion. Production managers of every background, from anywhere in Canada, are welcome to apply.
